newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan says raising cap on banks' stock holdings.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan says raising cap on banks' stock holdings.

text.p: Finance Minister Paul Chiu said on Wednesday that Taiwan would raise by the end of June the limit on banks' stock market holdings to 20 percent of a bank's net asset value from 15 percent.
Under the reform, banks also would be allowed for the first time to have holdings in Taiwan's fledgling over-the-counter market as well as corporate bonds, Chiu said.
"We will announce the measure, which will have immediate effect, by the end of June," Chiu told reporters before leaving for the Philippines for a meeting of Asia Pacific finance ministers.
Banks' total net asset value currently T$941.5 billion, or about US$34 billion, Chiu said.
Under the relaxation, the amount of that total net asset value that could be held in securities would rise to T$188 billion from T$141 billion.
The reform would be the latest in a string of financial sector liberalisations with the aim of establishing the island as an Asian capital centre.
